text: 23-year Del Mar resident with many years of service protecting our Community Plan: two terms as your Councilmember, 3 years on Finance Committee, 4 years on Sea Level Rise Advisory Committee, and 1.5 years on Design Review Board.
If re-elected, my top priorities are:
Consider the viewpoints of all residents before deciding how to vote. Work to find viable solutions.
Underground utilities for all neighborhoods as quickly as possible.
Relocate railroad tracks without tunnelling under Del Mar homes.
Local Control of land use decisions – follow our Community Plan.
Implement affordable housing plans that benefit our community.
Maintain our beaches through sand replenishment.
Safe railroad crossings to access bluff and beach.
Preserve Del Mar’s Bluffs, Beach, and Lagoon for future generations.
Since joining the Council, our successes include:
Utility undergrounding completed along south Stratford; underway or in design for Crest Canyon, north Stratford, and Beach Colony.
Updated Scenic View ordinance to protect property values and community character.
Rejected railroad fencing on Del Mar Bluffs.
Rejected Managed Retreat and nourished our sandy beaches.
Advanced plans for affordable housing at Fairgrounds.
Created fire evacuation plan for Crest Canyon neighborhoods.
Questions? Call, text, or email me: 858-717-4600, terryfordelmar@gmail.com.
I would be honored to have your vote.

text: I’m a Del Mar Planning Commissioner running for City Council because the next four years will shape our community for decades. I’m not running to represent one point of view. I’m running to bring people together around practical solutions that put Del Mar first.

I earned my undergraduate degree from UC Berkeley and graduated with honors from Georgetown Law. For 16 years, I practiced business litigation, resolving complex problems. I then led nonprofit organizations serving survivors of human trafficking and advancing environmental and educational initiatives. Effective leadership has defined my career.

After 25 years in Del Mar, I bring deep knowledge of local issues and an independent perspective. In the spirit of collegiality, I informed all four Councilmembers of my decision to run before announcing my candidacy.
My endorsements range from Del Mar Firefighters & Deputy Sheriffs’ Association to the Sierra Club and Congressman Mike Levin.
I’ll work to preserve local control, protect Del Mar’s interests in rail relocation, improve roads and infrastructure, strengthen fire and flood safety, and manage taxpayer dollars wisely.
Del Mar is where my husband and I raised four sons. It has given our family much. I’m here to give back.
Let’s shape Del Mar’s future together.

text: Del Mar is at a crossroads. This election will decide if we follow the Community Plan that has successfully guided our city for more than 50 years or choose expensive ideas that could create debt and weaken essential services. As a retired banker and former Finance Committee member, I know the importance of careful planning and financial discipline. Borrowing millions of dollars to speed up projects we are already paying for over time could put Del Mar at serious risk, especially if the economy slows down.

If elected, I will help rebuild strong relationships with regional agencies, find practical ways to meet State housing rules, support moving the train off the bluffs without tunneling under homes or businesses, protect our fast emergency response times, improve wildfire and sea-level-rise safety without managed retreat, and preserve Del Mar’s special character.

I believe City Council members should be good stewards of our land and put residents’ interests first. With no personal agenda, I will be a leader Del Mar deserves, serving with honesty, ethics, and integrity.
I would be grateful for your support. Learn more at Jas4DelMar.com.

text: I am a third generation Del Mar resident who cares deeply about our city and have been actively engaged in Del Mar’s civic life for years. Served on multiple committees for over 20 years, including over a decade as a Finance Committee appointee and past Chair. Understanding the City’s budget and resources is critical to understanding what Del Mar can and cannot do.
I endeavor to provide the best non-partisan guidance and advice to the best of my abilities.

I am a member of the Friends of Del Mar Bluffs which has led the legal fight against NCTD and SANDAG. I am dedicated to maintaining access to the Bluffs and Coast. I will never stop fighting for this.
Here are my priorities:
Listen to all voices with an open mind to serve the entire community.
Be consistent, trustworthy, and fair to everyone – treat everyone with respect.
Underground utilities throughout Del Mar.
Prevent eminent domain and tunneling during rail realignment.
Repair streets and infrastructure.
Vibrant, walkable downtown.
Ensure beach access and clean, healthy beaches.
Ensure North Bluff development fits Del Mar.
Build affordable housing that works for Del Mar.
Uphold the Community Plan.
If you have questions, email jeff@jgsturgis.com. I would be honored to have your vote.
